recommendation.summary: Across 125 stated assumption combinations, keep current system protects the highest worst-case customer NPV; pulse optimization minimizes the largest forgone NPV. These are different decision rules, not probabilities of success.

sampling_envelope.scope: Propagation of the supplied throughput-ratio sampling interval through the same economic model. Conditional on this circuit, noise model and selected assumption ranges; not a confidence interval for commercial performance.

stress.interpretation: Win coverage is the fraction of these equally spaced grid cells in which an option has the highest customer NPV. It is NOT a probability, forecast or confidence level. No distribution over assumptions is asserted.
stress.tie_rule: Keep current system wins exact ties first, followed by calibration, pulse and controls.
warnings: All case data are fictional. No new physics is simulated by this stress grid; it reuses the supplied matching benchmark.
Worst and best results are over the stated discrete assumption grid, not all possible hardware or business conditions.
Sampling bounds and assumption ranges have different meanings and are reported separately.

assumptions.label: Vendor upfront implementation cost
assumptions.rationale: Paid at time zero. Must include all vendor implementation and supplied-hardware cost; the case provides no vendor cost data.

assumptions.label: Vendor yearly support cost
assumptions.rationale: Paid at each contract-year end, including rollout years. Same hypothetical cost basis is applied to each proposal for comparison.

assumptions.label: Target nominal gross margin
assumptions.rationale: Defined as (nominal contract revenue - nominal delivery cost) / nominal revenue. Cash timing is checked separately.

assumptions.label: Vendor share of customer value
assumptions.rationale: Fraction of modeled gross customer value charged as the fee, on the same installment schedule. It is not the fraction retained by the customer.

warnings: Vendor costs, margin target and value-share policy are analyst assumptions, not facts from the fictional case.
All price floors and ceilings are nominal total fees on the same equal year-end installment schedule. Present values are labeled separately.
A positive quote must satisfy both the nominal margin target and vendor cash-flow break-even. Zero-price offers have no defined gross margin and are not recommended contracts.
The quoted controls hardware price is not its manufacturing cost. Enter the vendor's actual inclusive hardware and delivery cost before using this tool for that proposal.
Customer value remains conditional on the workload and valuation mode; this does not establish willingness to pay, market pricing, tax treatment or a vendor valuation.
